text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Diesel may rise three escudos per litre in the next two weeks but petrol prices will stay unchanged, a source from the petrol sector told the paper.
- Credit Lyonnais is negotiating the sale of its five percent stake in Banco Portugues de Investimento to one of the bank's major shareholders, the paper says.
- Government has two privatization plans for Airport Authority ANA. One sees it split into two companies, the other into three.
- Private mobile telephone company Telecel, state electricity concern EDP and gas company Transgas could join to create a second national telecommunications operator.

- Volkswagen to recall 21,000 Sharan multi-purpose vehicles (MPV) made at its AutoEuropa plant south of Lisbon because of a possible problems with the braking system and the door locks. The problem also involves the Ford Galaxies made at the joint venture with Ford but company officials could give no figure for the number of vehicles, the paper said.

- Tax on company profits will be reduced in 1997 by one percentage point to 35 percent. The government will adopt a proposal from the Portuguese Industry Confederation in return for its backing of a plan to levy a minimum tax on the self-employed and professional people.
- Government offers 2.375 percent pay rise to public sector workers. Portugal's main trade unions CGTP and UGT consider the proposal "unacceptable".
- Fertilizer company Quimigal Adubos privatization may be postponed to 1997.
- Transport companies fear new oil price rises in October 1997 and say the sector will be slashed to one third of its present size if the government does not help.
